title: review: G5: Jev gate in sampled mode by default — deterministic sampling, local exact-repeat detection without a network call, tool target and input hash in gate rows, and an offline diagnosis command with a labelling export
spec:
Depends on G1b (T-0265) and G2b (T-0267) because all three add cli.py subcommands. Scout T-0262: gate.jsonl rows carry ts, task, session, tool, p_needed, p_redundant, p_destructive, mode, blocked, latency_ms, scored, since F1 also startup_ms and rule, but no tool target or input hash, so repeated reads cannot be detected locally. Phase F measured 590 ms network per scored call and 62 to 78 percent 'redundant' verdicts on reviewers without knowing whether those reads were necessary verification.
Change:
1. jev_gate.py: [jev].gate_mode gains 'sample' (new default in pool.toml; log and block stay). In sample mode a call is scored only when sha1(session_id + call_index) mod 1000 < sample_rate * 1000 ([jev].sample_rate default 0.1); unscored calls make no network request. Every call, scored or not, computes tool_target (the path for Read/Edit/Write/Grep/Glob, the first 80 chars of the command for Bash, redacted through jev.redact) and input_hash = sha1(tool + normalised tool_input), and updates runs/jev/session-<session>.json {input_hash: {count, mtime}}; repeat = true when the same hash was seen in this session and the target file's mtime is unchanged. Rows gain tool_target, input_hash, repeat, sampled. In block mode, [jev].block_repeats = true (default false) denies a repeat with the message 'identical read already made this session; use the earlier result'. Startup stays one interpreter call; the hook script passes through unchanged apart from any new env it needs.
2. cli.py: `orchestrator jev diagnose [--since YYYY-MM-DD] [--export FILE --n N]`: from gate.jsonl and the bus (task -> role): calls, scored, sampled share, waste_pct by tool and by role, repeat rate by role, latency p50/p95 and startup vs network split, blocked count; --export writes N random scored rows with an empty label column as JSONL for hand labelling, and the command prints where.
3. pool.toml [jev]: gate_mode = "sample", sample_rate = 0.1, block_repeats = false, each with a comment; README Jev paragraph updated (sample mode, repeat detection, diagnose, labelling before any block).
Tests in tests/test_jev_gate.py: test_sample_mode_is_deterministic, test_unsampled_call_makes_no_request, test_repeat_detected_without_network, test_repeat_cleared_when_mtime_changes, test_rows_have_target_hash_and_flags, test_block_repeats_denies; tests/test_cli.py::test_jev_diagnose_summary (fixture gate.jsonl).
acceptance: pool.toml [jev] gate_mode is sample with sample_rate 0.1 and block_repeats false, documented; README updated
Existing tests pass; .claude/hooks/tests-green.sh exits 0 in the worktree

comments.issue: None of the six required tests (test_sample_mode_is_deterministic, test_unsampled_call_makes_no_request, test_repeat_detected_without_network, test_repeat_cleared_when_mtime_changes, test_rows_have_target_hash_and_flags, test_block_repeats_denies) exist anywhere in the repo. Grepping tests/ for all six names returns zero matches. The acceptance criteria name these as required to pass; since they don't exist, running those node ids fails outright and tests-green.sh cannot pass.

test_jev_diagnose_summary is also required by acceptance criteria but does not exist anywhere in tests/. The new `orchestrator jev diagnose` CLI subcommand in orchestrator/cli.py has no test coverage at all.

_record_call does a read-modify-write on .orchestrator/state/runs/jev/session-{id}.json with no file locking, unlike jev.py's own shared state (jev_state.json), which is guarded by STATE_LOCK_FILE. PreToolUse hooks for a single session can fire concurrently for parallel tool calls; concurrent invocations will race on this file, silently losing repeat-count updates (breaking block_repeats/repeat detection) and can interleave partial writes that json.loads then fails to parse, silently resetting session state to {} on the next read.

_target returns jev.redact(path) and that redacted string is what _target_mtime later calls os.stat() on (jev_gate.py:167). redact() is meant to scrub secret-shaped substrings before network egress/logging; if a real file path happens to match one of its patterns (e.g. a 32+ char alnum run, common in content-hashed build/cache directories), os.stat() silently fails on the mangled path and mtime is permanently None for that target, defeating 'repeat cleared when mtime changes' for that file without any error surfaced.
